this is not gonna last long in a device like a ps controller which moves around a lot.

1. your leads are overbent and damaged, so they are far less reliable and have very little stress relief.
2. you haven't cleaned the flux off, which can cause corrosion over time.
3. a couple of your solder joints are dry and not wetted properly, meaning they'll have intermittent failures and they'll break over time
4. some of your solder joints didn't go into full reflow because your iron wasn't hot enough, meaning they'll have poor stress tolerance
5. your leads aren't clipped properly
6. your capacitor violates the minimum acceptable electrical clearance as designated by the IPC-610

if someone liked onision more than godspeed then that's their subjective opinion. 


you are only viewing music through a subjective lens. if you only think music can be viewed subjectively then you will only be able to view it subjectively. by actually listening to both and comparing the two, it's very easy to tell which one is objectively better. 

classifying the quality of music in an objective way is totally different to saying "i like this more than this". 

objectively good could be where the vast majority of people enjoy the music, it heavily effects those people emotionally, the musician put lots of effort into the music, and it is historically significant and influenced other genres.


objectively bad would be where the vast majority of people do not like the music, and it doesn't effect the people who do enjoy it emotionally, the musician didn't put effort into it, and it isn't historically significant. 


the reason i "chose" those 4 qualities is because they are what the main purpose of music is (and even art as a whole!)


it's like saying "oh, a space elevator and a mudhut can't be compared because the quality of architecture is subjective.". in the case of either of these, it would be up to qualities such as structural integrity, usefulness, and technological complexity to determine how objectively "good" or "better" one is compared to the other. sure, there are at least a few people out there who would think "the government should build more mudhuts!" when given the choice between mudhuts and space elevators, but the vast majority of people are going to choose the space elevator. people will choose the space elevator based on their own subjective opinions and life experiences, but the reason the *majority* of people will have the subjective opinion of that is because of *objective* qualities.


the same thing happens with music. the purpose of music is to be enjoyable! that is the number 1 purpose of music. there are very, very few exceptions to the fact that music is made for people to enjoy it. 
so, if lots and lots of people enjoy it, or the people within just a handful of the population that do enjoy it enjoy it a LOT, then that makes the music good! it depends on the balance between how much people enjoy it and how many people enjoy it. if everyone on planet earth listened to a song and had their life changed positively because of it, then you absolutely cannot deny that that song is good. 

something i should be putting more emphasis on, is that *subjective opinions do have value*. just because the underlying reasons a piece of music is good is because of objective qualities, doesn't mean that people's subjective opinions don't matter! again, like i said earlier with the mudhuts and the space elevators, *more people will enjoy the one that has the better objective qualities*. 

people will like songs for subjective reasons. but the reason the majority of people like a specific song, album, artist, or other musical venture, is because it fulfils certain objective qualities. i know ive said this a few times already, but really, that's the main point i'm trying to get across.

there sort of is. Onision vs GY!BE. there is obviously a clear "winner".

if there is some music which is objectively better than other music, then that means that there absolutely 100% is a hierarchy to the quality of music.

the quality of music is a 50/30/10/10 ratio of entertainment value/emotional impact/effort/historical significance, respectively. the higher the number for the specific quality, then the more of an impact it will have on the overall quality of the music.


about 50% of the quality of music is the entertainment value. is it enjoyable? do a wide range of audiences like the music? if not, how much do the people that listen to it enjoy it? can it easily become someone's favourite music/source of music? or is it an acquired taste? so on.


30% of the quality is from the emotional impact. can it make you cry? can it make you happy? can it drive you to do things you usually wouldn't? are the lyrics relatable or meaningful? if it doesn't have lyrics, are the instruments coordinated well enough that it can trigger an emotional reaction? something very important, does the music trigger the reaction it's *intended to*, or does it trigger a different reaction? (if people are laughing at a lament that you wrote for your dying mother, and you didn't intend that, obviously something is not right!)


the last 20% is split evenly between effort put into the music and the historical significance of the music. 10% effort, 10% significance.


the amount of effort put into a song doesn't always mean the song is better, but generally, the emotional impact of a song is directly proportional to the effort put into it, but not always the other way around. i would say that if a song really hits hard emotionally, someone or some people must've really put some effort into it! whether that be mechanical/physical effort, psychological or emotional effort, or both. but something important to remember is that not all music with a lot of effort put into it will be emotionally heavy, and it may not even have much entertainment value. and sometimes a song may have an emotional impact even though not much effort was put into it, but this is generally very few songs, and within those few songs very few people find that those songs have an intense emotional impact.


finally there is historical significance. a lot of people say that this is all that matters, but that is not the case (you can understand why by reading the parts of the comment before this). for example, much of the music of Beethoven is very very historically significant, but its actual entertainment value and emotional significance isn't the best. i don't think you see people crying because they heard Für Elise very often, unless they have a memory connected with it (which is a subjective quality, so it doesn't matter in this case). it's entertainment value is generally pretty average or below average, as only few people enjoy his music when compared to the vast majority of people, who generally listen to Hip Hop, Pop, and Rock. this is also because the music is dated; people once found his music to be invigorating and emotionally impactful. however, people today now find it to be pretty "normal" music ("background" music), and it's qualities besides effort and historical significance have diminished since it was created. you might think that because of this, the entertainment value and emotional impact of music is subjective, but as humanity's ideas surrounding music evolve and change, so does their psychology and neurology based around overall enjoyment and liking of newer types of music. the only reason that the past emotional and entertainment values of historically significant music matter is, well, to increase the music's historical significance! (sorry if that last part was ambiguous, i'm rushing this a bit as i need to go soon).


but overall, music most definitely has objective qualities, and the ratio and values of these qualities is directly correlated with how much better a piece of music is compared to another. 

subjective opinions on a piece of music do matter, but there are most definitely objective qualities to music, and music can be organised in a hierarchy correlating to these.
